title: Guided Onboarding (Hosted API) — Success Metrics v1 (Jan 2026)
body:
Context
- Project: Guided onboarding experience + in-product “first production launch” checklist for Hosted API (Phase 1).
- Purpose of this doc: define the success metrics + measurement approach so we can (a) decide if the checklist works, (b) compare beta vs control cohorts, and (c) correlate onboarding completion with retention/usage.
- Owners:
  - PM: Nikhil (this doc)
  - Analytics: Mei Lin
  - Event schema / pipeline: Nadia Rahman + Logan Wright
  - Console instrumentation: Dylan Brooks / Console team


1) Primary success metrics (what we will optimize)

1.1 Median time-to-first-success (TTFS)
Definition
- TTFS = time from org signup (or first Console session for existing orgs) → first successful Hosted API response.
- “Successful Hosted API response” = gateway response status 2xx for a text/chat generation request (NOT embeddings in v1).
- For multi-project orgs: compute per project and roll up to org using earliest successful project.

How it will be measured (preferred)
- Start timestamp: event onboarding.signup_completed OR (fallback) auth.user_created + org_created timestamps.
- End timestamp: backend validator signal “first_successful_request_at” (server-computed) OR telemetry event api.request_succeeded with status=2xx.
- Metric output: median, p75, p90 (median is the headline).

Success criteria / target
- Baseline (Dec 2025 cohort estimate): median ~18–24 minutes; p90 ~2.5–4 hours. (Confirm with Mei from baseline dashboard.)
- Target (Phase 1 GA): reduce median by 20–30% and p90 by 10–20% without increasing support contacts per new signup.

Caveats
- Clock source mismatch if we use mixed client/server timestamps. Prefer server-computed end timestamp.
- Some users hit the API without visiting Console; we need a reliable “signup start” event in those cases (see Identity notes below).
- Free-trial abuse/bots can bias TTFS downward (fast scripted calls). We’ll apply a bot filter (see section 5.4).


1.2 Median time-to-first-production-launch (TTFPL)
Definition
- TTFPL = time from signup → completion of “first production launch” checklist group.
- “First production launch group complete” is a derived flag from checklist state (server-side): first_production_launch_completed_at.
- This is explicitly a product-defined activation metric, not “customer declares prod”. It indicates meeting our minimum bar for production readiness.

Minimum bar (v1, subject to PM-483)
- A) Prod-mode API key created (or existing prod key identified)
- B) Retries/timeouts configured (validated by SDK defaults OR user acknowledgement for non-SDK)
- C) Rate limits/quotas reviewed (at least visited relevant page; not necessarily changed)
- D) Observability basics completed (visited Usage dashboard + has request IDs enabled)
- E) Rollout/rollback guidance acknowledged (docs view + “I understand” confirmation)

How it will be measured
- Source of truth: checklist_state table (per org + project) with group completion timestamps.
- We will report both:
  - TTFPL among orgs that achieve it within 30 days
  - % achieving production launch within 7 / 14 / 30 days (more stable early on)

Success criteria / target
- Baseline: not available (feature doesn’t exist). We will establish baseline during beta via “shadow checklist” (non-UI) for a 1–2 week period if possible.
- Target (Phase 1 GA): +10–15pp increase in % of new orgs reaching production launch within 14 days.

Caveats
- This is a composite metric. Individual step definitions may shift slightly during beta; if we change step logic we must version metrics (v1 vs v1.1) and avoid mixing cohorts.


1.3 Onboarding completion rate (checklist funnel)
Definition
- Completion rate = % of eligible orgs that complete ALL checklist steps within a timeframe.
- Primary cut: within 7 days of signup (D7). Secondary: D1, D14, D30.

Eligibility (who is in denominator)
- New orgs only for headline completion (avoid backfilled validations for existing orgs).
- Exclude orgs that are enterprise-provisioned (sales-assisted) in Phase 1 metrics reporting (separate view).

Step-level metrics
- Step completion rate per step
- Median time between steps (step-to-step latency)
- Drop-off point distribution (which step is “first not completed”)

Success criteria / target
- D7 completion rate: +15–25% relative lift vs control cohort.
- Reduce biggest drop-off step by at least 20% relative.


2) Secondary success metrics (ensure we’re improving real outcomes)

2.1 Activation / early usage
We will measure:
- % of new orgs with ≥3 successful API calls on ≥2 distinct days within first 14 days (D14 “repeat usage”).
- Total tokens generated in first 7 days (with winsorization to cap extreme outliers).
- # of distinct models used in first 7 days (proxy for exploration; interpret carefully).

Target
- +5–10% relative lift in D14 repeat usage.

Caveats
- Token volume can increase because of bad behavior (loops/retries). Pair with error-rate and cost-per-successful-call.


2.2 Reliability + support burden (guardrail metrics)
We should NOT “win” onboarding by encouraging risky behavior.
Guardrails:
- Support tickets per 100 new orgs (from Zendesk/Jira intake tag “onboarding”)
- 401 rate in first 24h (wrong key / auth confusion)
- 429 rate in first 24h (quota misunderstanding)
- Streaming disconnect rate (if streaming step is emphasized)
- Refund/credit-appeasement rate for onboarding cohort (proxy for frustration)

Targets
- No regression in tickets per 100 new orgs.
- Reduce 401 wrong-key incidents by 20–30% once “test vs prod key” UX ships.


2.3 Qualitative signals
- In-product “Was this checklist helpful?” CSAT for new orgs after completing 3+ steps.
- Short free-text prompt (max 280 chars) with strict redaction rules (no prompts, no payloads). Security review required.


3) Metric definitions (canonical) + formulas

3.1 Entities and identity model
We will compute metrics at 3 levels:
- User (for UI interactions)
- Org (for signup + billing + overall conversion)
- Project (for API key + API usage + validators)

Identity stitching rules (v1)
- Primary key: org_id
- If a user signs up but doesn’t create a project, they count for signup but not for API usage denominators.
- If API calls happen before Console events, we still attach to org_id via API key → project_id → org_id mapping.


3.2 Definitions
- “Signup” timestamp (new orgs): org_created_at (auth DB) OR onboarding.signup_completed (client event). Prefer server.
- “First API key created”: first_api_key_created_at (server).
- “First request”: first_successful_request_at (server validator).
- “First streaming session”: first_streaming_session_at (server validator; definition: at least N streamed chunks over a single request_id, see event schema).
- “Visited usage dashboard”: onboarding.console_page_view where page=usage_dashboard (client).
- “Production key created”: api_key_created where key_env=prod.


3.3 Standard time windows
We will report metrics in these windows:
- D0–D1: within 24h
- D0–D7: within 7 days
- D0–D14: within 14 days
- D0–D30: within 30 days


4) Expected impact model (how we expect the checklist to move the numbers)
Hypotheses
H1: Checklist + deep links reduces “where do I start?” friction → lower TTFS
- Mechanism: user sees “Install SDK” + “Make first request” with copy + known-good snippets.
- Leading indicator: higher completion of first_request step; lower time from api_key_created → first_success.

H2: Explicit prod/test key step reduces 401s and wasted time
- Mechanism: key labeling + docs link reduces wrong-environment key usage.
- Leading indicator: fewer 401s flagged with reason=invalid_key_env (if available), reduced support ticket theme “401 wrong key”.

H3: Rate limit/quota education step reduces 429 loops and support contacts
- Mechanism: better expectations + recommended retry behavior.
- Leading indicator: lower 429 rate per org in first 24h (normalized by request count), and fewer tickets about quotas.

H4: Observability + request ID guidance increases self-serve debugging and reduces tickets
- Mechanism: pushing users to Usage dashboard + request IDs.
- Leading indicator: higher usage_dashboard_visit rate; fewer “cannot debug” tickets; faster resolution times.


5) Measurement approach, caveats, and quality checks

5.1 Beta experiment design (recommended)
- Cohorts:
  - Control: checklist feature flag OFF
  - Treatment: checklist feature flag ON
- Randomization unit: org_id at signup (avoid cross-contamination across users within org)
- Ramp: 10% → 25% → 50% of new orgs (per Marissa / releases)
- Report: weekly readout with Mei + Nikhil; include both metrics + telemetry health.


5.2 Validation lag
- Some validators are server-computed off logs/metrics (possible lag 1–10 minutes).
- For TTFS, this is acceptable; we’ll report in minutes/hours and focus on medians.
- We need a “validation_lag_seconds” field in derived tables for QA.


5.3 Event loss / regional gaps
- Telemetry can fail per region (we’ve seen this historically). We will:
  - Prefer server-side validators for core steps
  - Maintain a daily event volume monitor by region
  - Provide a fallback computation path for TTFS from gateway logs if client events are missing


5.4 Bot / abuse filtering (new org cohorts)
Exclude orgs from headline onboarding metrics if any of:
- >X requests in first 10 minutes AND no Console session within 24h
- Disposable email domain + extreme token volume in first 1h
- Known fraud labels from billing risk (if available)

Note: still keep a “full population” view for engineering telemetry health checks.


5.5 Metric versioning
- Any change to step definitions, validator logic, or checklists requires:
  - metric_version field (e.g., onboarding_metrics_v1)
  - cohort annotations (start_date/end_date)
  - avoid comparing across versions without adjustment


6) Dashboards + queries (working links)
Note: Links are placeholders until Mei publishes final dashboards. Use internal access only.

6.1 Onboarding funnel dashboard (primary)
- Dashboard: Redwood Metrics / Product / Guided Onboarding (Hosted API)
- Link: https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/dashboards/PRD-GO-001
- Tabs:
  - New org funnel (signup → key → first request → streaming → prod key → usage dashboard → production launch)
  - Step drop-off analysis
  - Time-to metrics (TTFS, time between steps)

Key queries
- Q1: New org cohort definition
  - https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/queries/GO-101 (new_orgs_by_day)
- Q2: TTFS distribution
  - https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/queries/GO-102 (ttfs_minutes_by_org)
- Q3: Step completion rates (D7)
  - https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/queries/GO-103 (step_completion_d7)


6.2 Reliability guardrails dashboard
- Dashboard link: https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/dashboards/PRD-GO-002
- Q4: 401/429 rates in first 24h
  - https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/queries/GO-201
- Q5: Streaming disconnect rate
  - https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/queries/GO-202


6.3 Telemetry health dashboard (owned by Logan/Nadia)
- Dashboard link: https://metrics.redwoodinference.internal/dashboards/OBS-GO-001
- Monitors:
  - event ingestion volume by region
  - dedupe key collision rate
  - pipeline delay p50/p95


7) Open questions / TODO
- Do we want TTFS to count “any endpoint” (chat/embeddings/rerank) or only chat/text? Proposal: v1 = chat/text only; add embeddings in v1.1.
- Should “first production launch” require a minimum volume (e.g., 100 successful requests) to avoid “checkbox completion”? Proposal: no for Phase 1; keep simple.
- How do we attribute improvements to checklist vs improved docs/snippets? Proposal: still treat as one initiative for Phase 1; measure doc-link UTM clickthrough as a secondary diagnostic.
- Confirm if we can tag support tickets reliably with “onboarding” + “checklist” tags (Dev Patel / Priya Shah to confirm).


Appendix A: Quick glossary
- TTFS: time-to-first-success (signup → first 2xx API call)
- TTFPL: time-to-first-production-launch (signup → production checklist group complete)
- D7 completion: completed within 7 days of signup

Appendix B: Notes from working session (Jan 28)
- Mei: prefer server-derived validator timestamps; client events are “best effort”.
- Logan: needs property allowlist finalized before dashboards are locked.
- Marissa: beta cohort will start with new orgs only; existing orgs later to avoid skew.
